cases.canonicalQuestion: Does delaying an ARO cancel Hidden Deployment or Camouflaged State?
cases.draftAnswer: Delaying an ARO with a Trooper in Hidden Deployment cancels Hidden Deployment. By contrast, merely delaying an ARO with a Camouflaged Marker does not cancel Camouflaged State; that state is canceled only when one of its listed cancellation conditions occurs.
cases.approvedAnswer: Delaying an ARO with a Trooper in Hidden Deployment cancels Hidden Deployment. By contrast, merely delaying an ARO with a Camouflaged Marker does not cancel Camouflaged State; that state is canceled only when one of its listed cancellation conditions occurs.

cases.canonicalQuestion: What is a Tacball and how does it work?
cases.draftAnswer: A Tacball is a stationary Deployable Weapon used by Team-Ops Units. It declares a BS Attack or CC Attack against any Order declared by an active enemy Model—but not a Marker—within its Line of Fire or in Silhouette contact. It has Total Reaction, a Combi Rifle, and a PARA CC Weapon (-3). It does not activate other Deployable Weapons or Equipment, is removed after suffering Wounds equal to its STR 1, and must be represented by a 55 mm Tacball Token or another S4 model or scenery piece.

cases.canonicalQuestion: How does Request a Tacball work?
cases.draftAnswer: Request a Tacball is an Optional Attack Short Skill available only to a Trooper with Infinity Team-Ops, and it can be used only in the second Game Round. It requires no Roll. The Trooper places a 55 mm Tacball Token in Silhouette contact with any part of its route, chooses one unique, non-transferable item from the Tacball Chart, and applies that item at the end of the Order. The Token is Deployable Equipment and remains where deployed until the game ends, it is destroyed, or it is removed. Each player may use this Skill only once per game.

cases.canonicalQuestion: Can a model squeeze through a gap if it is along the table edge?
cases.approvedAnswer: It depends on the Skill. Move: Yes, provided at least half of the base remains supported throughout, the available surface is at least half the base's width, and the entire base fits at the end of the Move. Climb or Climbing Plus: Yes, provided at least half of the base's underside remains in contact with the vertical surface and the Trooper can finish on a surface large enough for the entire base; the rules do not say that the whole Silhouette must remain inside the physical table boundary. Jump or Super-Jump: The table-edge issue is not explicitly resolved. The complete Silhouette must follow the declared trajectory without passing through scenery, and the entire base must fit on the horizontal landing spot, but the rules do not state whether part of the airborne trajectory may extend beyond the physical table boundary. Agree before the game or obtain a tournament-organizer ruling for Jump at the table edge.

cases.canonicalQuestion: Can I dodge sideways during an impetuous activation?
cases.approvedAnswer: It depends on the route; Dodge is not unrestricted during an Impetuous activation. Dodge has the Movement label, so Impetuous movement restrictions apply even though Move + Dodge is allowed. First reach Silhouette contact with an enemy if possible; otherwise move towards the enemy Deployment Zone without doubling back, following the Impetuous movement priorities. A sideways Dodge is legal only if it satisfies those restrictions, for example by reaching an enemy beside you. Once inside the enemy Deployment Zone, movement is normal provided you stay inside it. Dodge uses its own movement allowance, not the Move Skill distance. These Impetuous Phase restrictions do not apply merely because a trooper has Impetuous when Dodging in ARO or during a regular Order.

cases.canonicalQuestion: what is the interaction of a msv1 shooting and msv1 through smoke? And what modifiers to both parties get?
cases.approvedAnswer: It depends on the response. If both MSV1 troopers shoot at each other through ordinary Smoke, each takes a -3 Visibility MOD: each is targeted by a BS Attack, treats the Smoke as Poor Visibility when drawing LoF to the attacker, and MSV1 reduces its -6 MOD to -3. If the target Dodges instead, the MSV1 shooter takes -6; Dodge is not a return BS Attack. Dodge takes no Visibility Zone MOD, although other Dodge MODs may apply. Merely having MSV1 on both models does not remove the Smoke penalty. These are visibility modifiers only; apply Range, Cover and other applicable MODs separately. This assumes no special exception such as Sixth Sense, and does not apply to Eclipse or White Noise.

approvedCitations.section: VISIBILITY CONDITIONS — ZERO AND POOR VISIBILITY

cases.canonicalQuestion: do Mines trigger against engaged models?
cases.approvedAnswer: Already Engaged with the Mine owner's ally: no trigger, because a template on that combat affects everyone involved, including the ally. Moving into contact: the Mine triggers at a valid position before contact if the enemy is inside its Trigger Area and the template can hit it without affecting any ally. Ending the Move Engaged does not undo that earlier legal trigger. If the only valid position is after contact, or every template would affect an ally, it does not trigger. LoF alone is insufficient: the enemy must be within the Trigger Area and not in Total Cover from the template's Blast Focus. Dodge movement itself does not trigger Mines; however, declaring Dodge while already inside the Trigger Area can trigger one if the normal conditions are met. These distinctions assume the close combat includes an ally of the Mine's owner.

approvedCitations.section: MINES — TRIGGER CONDITIONS, ALLIES AND DODGE MOVEMENT

cases.canonicalQuestion: Can a player Request a Tacball if only one player has Team-Ops?
cases.approvedAnswer: Yes. Request a Tacball is available to a Trooper with Infinity Team-Ops and does not require the opponent to have Team-Ops. It may be used only in the second Game Round and only once per player per game. However, Tacball Classified Objectives are a separate ITS Extra: they are used only if both players have Team-Ops Units in their Army Lists. Therefore, with Team-Ops on only one side, that player may Request and deploy a Tacball, but neither player rolls or replaces a Classified Objective from the Tacball Classified Objectives Chart.

cases.canonicalQuestion: Can a CrazyKoala trigger on a Camouflage Marker?
cases.approvedAnswer: No. CrazyKoalas are Perimeter Weapons, and Perimeter Weapons do not trigger on Camouflage Markers (CAMO), Impersonation Markers (IMP-1 or IMP-2), or any Marker whose rules say so. The CrazyKoala can trigger only after the trooper is no longer represented by one of those protected Markers and otherwise meets its normal trigger conditions.

cases.canonicalQuestion: Can a CrazyKoala be placed with an enemy Camouflage Marker inside its Zone of Control?
cases.approvedAnswer: Only if there is also a valid, non-Camouflaged enemy inside the CrazyKoala's Trigger Area. Place Deployable normally cannot place a Deployable Weapon when an enemy Camouflage Marker is in its Trigger Area; the stated exception is when a valid non-Camouflaged enemy is also inside that area. A CrazyKoala is Deployable and Perimeter, so it is placed totally inside its owner's Zone of Control rather than in Silhouette contact. It still does not trigger on the Camouflage Marker itself.

cases.canonicalQuestion: Can a Trooper with Aerial benefit from Deployable Cover?
cases.approvedAnswer: No. While Aerial is active, the Trooper is never in Silhouette contact with scenery or other game elements, even if it is physically touching them. Partial Cover requires contact with the scenery that obscures the Trooper, and Deployable Cover applies that Partial Cover rule. The Vitroferro Saving Roll bonus also expressly requires Silhouette contact. Therefore an active Aerial Trooper cannot claim either Deployable Cover variant's Cover benefits.

cases.canonicalQuestion: Does a WildParrot trigger when an enemy Camouflaged Marker inside its Trigger Area chooses not to declare an ARO?
cases.approvedAnswer: No. A deployed WildParrot works like an E/M Mine. A Mine triggers when an enemy Model or Marker declares or executes a Skill or ARO inside its Trigger Area. Merely being eligible for an ARO and choosing not to declare one is not a declared or executed Skill or ARO; the Marker instead loses its ARO against that Order. Therefore the WildParrot does not trigger from the waived ARO alone. If the Marker actually declares or executes a Skill or ARO in the Trigger Area, the WildParrot must trigger if its template can legally affect that enemy without affecting an ally.
